name: the opera glass
beats: A small French opera glass in brass and black enamel, bought for the opera and used for everything else; it brings the far kerb to arm's length.

name: the old man by the cab rank
beats: About sixty, in a decent coat too heavy for August, standing at the kerb heels together and chin up, as though told to stand there and not yet told to stop.
He leans on the stick in his left hand harder than a man of his years would wish, and when he steps aside for a perambulator the left leg swings stiff from the hip, the knee hardly bending.
His neck, below the line of a cap he no longer wears, is burned a deep brick colour that no English summer gives a man.

name: the clergyman
beats: A long black coat gone shiny at the seams, the cuffs turned, a white tie, and a good hat gone to the bad.
He reads a small book with his lips moving, and now and then looks up over the crowd as a man does who is repeating something to himself.
At this distance the book is only a small dark thing in his hand, and his face under the hat brim is too far off to make out.

name: the open window
beats: Both sashes are thrown up; below, Baker Street is thick with the holiday crowd, a cab rank along the far kerb and the chemist's window opposite.

name: the holiday crowd
beats: The crowd moves along the pavement in its hundreds, straw hats and children and a sailor among them, and nobody in it looks up.

name: the violin
beats: Holmes's violin in its case on the chair; he has been at it, on and off, since Saturday.

name: the monograph
beats: Holmes's monograph upon the ashes of the various tobaccos: a hundred and forty varieties, with coloured plates.
document: Upon the Distinction between the Ashes of the Various Tobaccos. By Sherlock Holmes. With coloured plates.
